title: The session-start peers line sits above the sprint lines, so the hook's 1000-character cap cuts every sprint line when the checkout lags
goal: The session-start hook keeps at least the first sprint line under its 1000-character cap when the checkout-lag line and the peers line are both present, the peers line being cut before any sprint line, and a check plants a lag line, a peers line and an active sprint and finds a sprint line in the hook's systemMessage

run: import json,subprocess,sys; m=json.loads(subprocess.run([sys.executable,"_tools/backlog.py","horizon","--hook"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)["systemMessage"]; sys.exit(0 if "sprint SP-" in m else 1)

import json, subprocess, sys
child = """
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_view, backlog
bl_view.lag_line = lambda root: "checkout is 12 commit(s) behind and 3 ahead of origin/main, so its hooks run old code and a fast-forward refuses: ask the operator about a rebase or merge onto origin/main"
bl_view.peers_line = lambda root: "peers: s-805a16 (topic plan), unbound (topic bl_peers.py) +1; before planning: python3 _tools/backlog.py peers"
sys.exit(backlog.main(["horizon", "--hook", "--all"]))
"""
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", child], capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8")
m = json.loads(p.stdout)["systemMessage"]
print(m[:400])
sys.exit(0 if p.returncode == 0 and ("sprint SP-" in m or "backlog: no active sprint" in m) and m.startswith("checkout is") else 1)
